source_text: Non igitur: "Tota disputatione tua contrivisti - sicut te iactas - assertionem meam, de malo carnalis concupiscentiae originalisque peccati"; … De testimoniis etiam tractatorum catholicorum sancti Basilii Caesareensis et sancti Ioannis Constantinopolitani, quorum dixisti sensum vestris convenire sententiis, in primo huius mei operis libro, tibi sufficientissima et certissima veritate respondi … In secundo quoque libro satis egimus, ut appareat quam non sit, quemadmodum conviciaris, "conspiratio perditorum" … Unde etiam "populi murmur, quod solum vobis a nobis - dicis - opponi", nec solum est, quia tantorum nititur auctoritate doctorum
pass_a_gloss: Not therefore: 'By your whole disputation you have crushed, as you boast, my assertion about the evil of carnal concupiscence and of original sin'. About the testimonies also of the catholic treatise-writers Saint Basil of Caesarea and Saint John of Constantinople, whose sense you said to agree with your (plural) opinions, in the first book of this work of mine I answered you with most sufficient and most certain truth. In the second book also we did enough, so that it appears how it is not, as you revile, 'a conspiracy of the lost'. Whence also 'the murmur of the people, which alone, you say, is opposed to you by us', is not alone, because it rests on the authority of such great doctors.
pass_b_english: Augustine reports, speaking to Julian: “So you have not, by your whole argument, crushed, as you boast, my assertion about the evil of fleshly desire and of original sin.”

“About the testimonies of the catholic writers Saint Basil of Caesarea and Saint John of Constantinople, whose meaning you said agrees with your views, I answered you in the first book of this work of mine with truth entirely sufficient and certain.”
“In the second book too we did enough to make it plain that it is not, as you abusively call it, ‘a conspiracy of lost men’ …”
“Hence also ‘the murmur of the people, which alone,’ you say, ‘is set against you by us,’ is not alone, since it rests on the authority of such great teachers …”

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.

choices.choice: The old English printed 'Throughout your whole argument you have crushed — as you boast — my assertion…' on its own as Julian's words. The Latin opens 'Non igitur:', and 'assertionem meam de malo carnalis concupiscentiae' is Augustine's own thesis, so the sentence is Augustine denying Julian's boast; now translated in Augustine's voice.

2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-d): the old English summarised Augustine's report ('Augustine reports that Julian ...') instead of translating it. Now a translation of the Latin clause(s) that carry Julian's words or Augustine's report of them, with Augustine named as speaker where the words are his; nothing added that the Latin does not say. Omitted stretches inside a paragraph are marked with an ellipsis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here. This row translates Augustine's report addressed to Julian, with Augustine named as speaker; Julian's words are the quoted parts.
